subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Leadership, Coaching, and Inclusive Event Design
essentialQuestion: How do I design an activity where the least confident person present has a good time?

prompts.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of coaching a skill to someone at a different level in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe designing an event for genuinely mixed abilities using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply safety planning and responsibility as an organizer in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving inclusive language, format, and scoring choices; correct it and explain why.
Connect handling conflict, dropout, and unexpected constraints with evaluating an event against inclusion rather than turnout and explain how one affects the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Design and facilitate one small inclusive activity session, then evaluate it against stated inclusion and safety criteria and revise the design.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

adaptationChoices: The session may be run for one person, for a household group, or delivered as a complete plan with a rehearsed walk-through if no participants are available.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
